eventMetadata.context_description: Official AEMET guidance forecasts a Madrid maximum of 37°C on August 8 under persistent high pressure, clear skies, and light winds that enhance daytime solar heating across the city's continental climate zone. Traders assign 65% implied probability to 38°C and 27% to 39°C because short-range ensemble models show modest warming potential above the official value, compounded by urban heat-island effects that routinely add 1–2°C in central districts. Late-summer climatology supports baseline highs near 32–34°C, yet current subsidence and dry air mass favor modest exceedance without frontal moderation. Resolution hinges on the single highest reading from official stations, with minimal forecast spread expected before the 24-hour window closes.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent MetService guidance and supporting model consensus point to a 14°C daily maximum for Wellington on August 9 under a northerly flow that draws milder maritime air ahead of a front. Occasional rain early in the day could limit solar heating and cap the peak near the seasonal average of 12–14°C, while stronger afternoon winds and partial clearing introduce modest upside potential toward 15°C. NIWA’s winter outlook assigns the highest probability to near-average temperatures across the lower North Island, consistent with the narrow market spread between the two leading outcomes and the low implied odds for extremes. Updated regional forecasts and any last-minute model adjustments ahead of resolution will determine whether the high settles at 14°C or edges higher.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current forecast models from sources including AccuWeather and regional services show Guangzhou maximum temperatures on August 9 likely reaching 37–38°C under the influence of a persistent subtropical high-pressure system promoting subsidence and clear to partly cloudy skies. This aligns with climatological August highs near 34°C that occasionally spike higher due to urban heat island effects in the densely built city. Trader consensus reflected in the 51.5% implied probability on 38°C and 23.5% on 37°C incorporates these factors along with limited model spread and typical day-to-day stability, while lower-probability outcomes above 39°C or below 36°C account for potential convective cooling or measurement variability. Updated guidance from the China Meteorological Administration over the next 24–48 hours will be the key catalyst for any shifts.
